summary: A standalone expansion/companion to One Night Ultimate Werewolf that adds eleven new roles with more elaborate abilities, keeping the same single-night, no-elimination, vote-to-win structure. It can be played alone or merged with the original for bigger, more chaotic groups.
praised: adds welcome variety and new role interactions to keep the format fresh
still fast and easy to run via the companion app
combines seamlessly with the base game for larger player counts
criticised: more roles mean more rules overhead for what's meant to be a quick filler
some new roles can be unbalanced or confusing for newcomers
same reliance on group bluffing skill as the base game, for better or worse

interaction.kind: hidden-role deduction, accusation, and a single group vote deciding everyone's fate
interaction.detail: As an expansion adding more roles to the same One Night format, it keeps the identical structure of secret night actions followed by open accusation and a single collective vote. Every player's fate hinges entirely on how well they read and argue with the others, with no individual board or private track.
interaction.said: "you have to convince everyone else you're not the werewolf", accusation and bluffing are the entire game

scoring.how_you_win: Same one-night structure as the base game: after night abilities resolve (now including Daybreak roles like the Alpha Wolf or Bomber), players discuss and cast simultaneous lynch votes; the village team wins if a Werewolf dies, Werewolves win if not, and certain solo roles win under their own special condition instead.
